title: Motion Machine sound sample record (SPEC §9): where a sound file came from
description: Every sample a style or story maps to a cue (`sound.samples`, `audio.samples`) has a record beside it: `assets/sounds/x.wav` has `assets/sounds/x.json`. A sample with no valid record is warned by W-SAMPLE-LICENSE. `mm sound mine` writes the same three fields for every sound it cuts out of a recording, so a mined sound that is kept as a sample already has its record (copy records/<id>.json beside the wav; the other fields are measurements, which a record may carry).

source.description: where the file came from: a page, a pack, a recording session, or `own recording`

licence.description: the terms it may be used under, as the source states them (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, a purchased licence, `own recording`)

author.description: who made the sound; the person themselves for an own recording

openverseId.description: a sound found on Openverse (`mm sound fetch`): its id there. With `source: "openverse"`, W-SAMPLE-LICENSE also judges the licence against what the piece offers, the sha1 against the file, and one recording against a second licence

licenceVersion.description: the licence's version as Openverse states it (4.0)

creator.description: who made it, as Openverse gives it; `author` carries the same name (or `unknown`)

landingUrl.description: the item's own page at its source, where its licence can be read again

attribution.description: the credit line Openverse composed for the item; `mm credits` prints it

provider.description: the catalogue Openverse found it in

sha1.description: the hash of the file as fetched: W-SAMPLE-LICENSE warns when the file no longer matches
